label: prop:kelvin-dispersion-derivation
title: Kelvin wave dispersion from the $q$-Laplacian eigenvalue problem
html:
The discrete vortex spectrum identifies the q-Laplacian eigenvalues on a vortex filament of length L. On the circle they are

  \lambda_k^{(q)} = [k]_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{L_q^2},
  \qquad
  [k]_q = \frac{q^k - q^{-k}}{q - q^{-1}},

the exact eigenvalues \mu_k^{(q)} = [k]_q^2 of \Delta_q on L-periodic functions (with L_q = L). The linearised q-Navier--Stokes equation for normal displacements then yields the q-deformed Kelvin dispersion and its viscous decay rate,

  \omega_k^{(q)}
  = 
  \frac{\Gamma_q^{1/2}}{2\sqrt{\pi}a_q}
  \frac{[k]_q}{L_q},
  \qquad
  \gamma_k^{(q)}
  = 
  \frac{\nu_q}{2}\frac{[k]_q^2}{L_q^2}
  = 
  \frac{\hbar_q}{4}\frac{[k]_q^2}{L_q^2},

where \Gamma_q = [j]_q[j+1]_q is the quantised circulation at intensity level j and a_q the q-deformed core radius. Because [k]_q \sim q^k at large k, mode k decays on the timescale \tau_k = 4L_q^2 / (\hbar_q[k]_q^2) — high modes decay doubly exponentially in k, the rigorous exponential UV cutoff built into the q-Navier--Stokes definition.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
